priceCaption: Base specification price, customisations quoted separately.
opener: A labour shed is the open-hall version of SAMAN worker housing: one clear sleeping hall per floor with central aisles, built as a light portal-frame steel building with PPGI cladding and high-level ventilation. It suits contractors who need the highest bed count per rupee and manage the hall as one space. The hall comes in six sizes, 60x24 ft G+1 up to 120x24 ft G+2, sleeping 58 to 216 workers a building. The hall is priced ex-factory on one per-square-foot rate, delivered in 7 to 21 working days with zoned lighting and emergency circuits fitted.
descriptionHtml:
The labour shed is built around one idea: maximum bunks under one supervised roof at minimum cost. Each floor is a single clear hall, no internal walls, with facing bed rows split by an aisle that runs end to end. A light portal-frame structure keeps the span open, PPGI cladding keeps the weather out, and continuous ventilator banks up high keep air crossing the hall without fans fighting the heat load alone.

Because the hall is one space, everything about running it is simpler. From the doorway one supervisor counts every bed. Cleaning is one crew and one pass. Re-allocating beds between crews is a list change, not a room change. Fire exits, emergency lighting and zoned circuits are engineered for open-hall occupancy from the first drawing, which is what separates a compliant shed from a shed-shaped problem.

The building arrives as fabricated components and stands in days on a prepared base, with an RCC slab preferred at high occupancies. Zoned lighting lets night-shift workers sleep while the day shift dresses. If your site needs lockable rooms rather than a hall, the hutment room block serves that brief; if the housing must move between projects, the relocatable camp build does. And to weigh all three types on one page, the worker housing range compares them side by side. This page is for the contractor whose priority is simply beds, delivered fast, at the lowest cost per worker housed.
